content.text: Cash-out is the feature I use most. Backed a side at 2.05 pre-match, they win the toss and the price drops to 1.45? I take the small profit and stop thinking about it. The button is honest about the number too — it shows the offer clearly before you confirm, and I've never had it move on me mid-tap.
Two formats are available, and you switch between them in account settings.
Decimal (the default): multiply your stake by the number to see the total return.
1.50 → ৳100 stake returns ৳150 (৳50 profit)
2.00 → ৳100 stake returns ৳200 (৳100 profit)
4.50 → ৳100 stake returns ৳450 (৳350 profit)
Fractional: the British style. 3/1 means ৳3 profit for every ৳1 staked, plus your stake back.
Quick sanity check: divide 1 by the decimal price to get the implied chance.
If your own read on a match says a team wins more often than that implied number, you've found a bet worth placing. If not, walk away — there's another match tomorrow.

content.text: None of this is advice, it's just the routine that stopped me from doing anything stupid over the last two seasons.
1. Stick to what you watch. I bet cricket and a bit of football. Adding six more sports just means guessing in six more places.
2. Cap each bet at 5% of the balance. With ৳10,000 in the account, that's ৳500 maximum. Dull, but it keeps you alive through a bad week.
3. Take the cash-out. Twice my stake showing on a live cricket bet? I press the button and move on.
4. No loyalty bets. Backing Bangladesh with my heart cost me more than any bookmaker ever did.
5. Write it down. Date, match, stake, price, result. Two months of notes will tell you honestly whether you're any good.
The rule that matters most: when you're ahead, withdraw. Up ৳4,000 on a Thursday night? Send ৳3,500 to bKash and shut the app. Rolling it into one more parlay is how good nights turn bad.
